question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(\frac{\pi }{4})=1,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ we have

$$
{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(\frac{5\pi }{18})$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=\frac{5\pi }{18}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{5\pi }{18}) & ≈L(\frac{5\pi }{18}) \\  & =1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\frac{5\pi }{18}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{36} \\  & =1+\frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{72}.\end{aligned}
$$
